title: Moly rule
description: One rule: what to look for in a unit of text, why it fails the reader, and how to fix it.

id.description: PACK-AREA-NNN. Stable forever. Retire an id; never reuse it.

title.description: The failure, stated as a fact about the text.

area.description: Pack-defined grouping. The letter in the id abbreviates it.

severity.description: block: the text does not do its job. warn: it does its job badly. note: it could do it better.

kind.description: mechanical: patterns decide, no model needed. judged: a model answers a question and must quote evidence.

scope.description: Unit types from the pack's units list that this rule reads.

patterns.description: Regular expressions, case-insensitive unless the rule sets case: true. Any match is a hit. Required for mechanical rules.

unless.description: Regular expressions that cancel a pattern hit on the same unit.

prefilter.description: Judged rules only. Cheap patterns that select candidate units so the model reads fewer of them. A unit that matches none is not a candidate.

question.description: Judged rules only. The yes/no question the model answers about one unit. Yes means a hit.

evidence.description: Judged rules only. What the model must quote to support a yes. A finding without this evidence is invalid.

explain.description: Why this fails the reader. Voice-neutral. The pack's voice layer may restyle it; it may not change the claim.

template.description: rewrite: the shape of the corrected text, with <angle> slots.

steps.description: procedure: ordered steps the agent or author follows.

touches_tests.description: True when applying the fix changes text that tests may assert on.

when.description: The condition under which the text may stand.

marker_required.description: Whether the author must mark the exception inline.

examples.description: The rule's contract. Mechanical rules must hit every hit and miss every pass. Judged rules use them to calibrate the model.

see.description: Related rule ids or source references.

context.description: Surrounding code or prose the judge needs. Optional.

reader.description: Who reads this unit: user, developer, operator, model.

note.description: Why this is a hit or a pass. Teaches the judge.
